newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - March 19.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - March 19.

text.p: THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

More than A$1 billion has been slashed from News Corporation's market capitalisation following its announcement of a A$1.6 billion deal to purchase United States marketing services group Heritage Media Corp. The deal will be funded through the issue of further preference shares. Page 1.

Figures released by the Australian Bureau of Statistics show Australia's housing industry has picked up in recent months and is now well on the road to recovery. Housing starts jumped 5.9 percent to around 30,500 in the December 1996 quarter after seasoal adjustment. Page 5.

In a bid to secure the sale of rail operator Australian National within the 1996-97 Budget year, the Federal Government has imposed a tight timetable for the A$600 million privatisation of the service. A deadline of June 30 has been set for the Office of Asset Sales and advisers Deutsche Morgan Grenfell to bed down private sector buyers.
Page 5.

Following speculation this week over the sale of Qantas Airways Ltd's share in Air New Zealand Ltd, the Qantas board is expected to meet today to consider a proposal to unload its 19.4 per cent stake in the Kiwi carrier, possibly to United States investor, for NZ$425.6 million. Wire services reported yesterday that Qantas' 112 million shares were close to being placed in the US at NZ$3.80 a share. Page 19.

Private-sector utilities were shocked yesterday as New South Wales Government-owned electricity distributor Great Southern Energy was able to outbid rivals such as AGL and Boral Energy to purchase the Wagga Wagga City Council's natural gas business for A$6 million, twice the market rate. Page 19.

MIM Holdings Ltd's Mt Isa operations manager Phil Wright has parted from the company, just three weeks after the surprise departure of exploration manager Ross Fardon. The resignations follow a major restructuring effort by managing director Nick Stump, who now has only eight executives, not 12, reporting to him. Page 19.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation Ltd has strengthened its position in the United States advertising and promotions industry with its A$1.7 billion purchase of Dallas-based supermarket promotion group Heritage Media. Heritage is also News Corp's main competitor in the fast-expanding coupons business. Page 19.

In its latest Australian Commodities publication, the Australian Bureau of Agriculture and Resource Economics says it expects a rise in minerals and energy exports, yet warns that the move to a single European currency could adversely affect some of Austrlia's commodities exports to the European Union. Page 19.

As the dollar gold price fell to its lowest level for 1997 yesterday, the Association of Mining and Exploration Companies has announced it intends to make a powerful submission to the West Australian Government against its plans for a gold tax. AMEC chief executive George Savell said the industry will not be defeated. Page 19.

Resource stocks involved in Papua New Guinea have recovered from their slump on Monday following an easing of fears of political unrest in the Pacific nation. Investor confidence was spurred by news of the sacking of the country's military chief, with Lihir Gold Ltd stock rising two cents to A$2.12, Orogen Minerals Ltd losing even at A$3.20, and Oil Search Ltd lifting 10
cents to A$2.70. Page 20.

Indonesian Trade Minister Tunky Ariwibowo has approached BHP to look at gaining a stake in State-owned steel maker Krakatau Steel. BHP has been involved in Indonesia since the early 1970s, and is considered an ideal partner in the State steel arm, which lans to raise A$800 million in an initial share offering this year.
Page 21.

It is unlikely there will be a repeat of low earnings for BHP's Steel division in the third-quarter, which last year denied BHP's overall profits. The Big Australian is expecting to benefit from BHP Steel's generally buoyant figures released yesterday, wth an estimated third-quarter profit of between A$310 million and A$330 million.
Page 21.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD
Financial institutions are introducing new products and higher interest rates in an effort to attract customers to the retail deposit market.

The moves, which replicate those needed to compete in the intense home loan industry, have seen Colonial State Bank, National Australia Bank, AMP's PriorityOne and GIO Australia revamp their deposit products. Page 29.

News Corp announced yesterday it would issue A$950 million of its non-voting preferred stock and take on an extra A$750 million of debt to buy Heritage Media Corp, its main competitor in the United States supermarket coupon business, for A$1.7 billion. The move was not greeted well by investors, who wrote A$1 billion off the company's market capitalisation. Page 29.

MIM's share price fell five cents to A$1.72 yesterday as the surprise resignation of high-profile Mt Isa operations executive general manager Phil Wright was announced. While analysts are unsure whether Wright's resignation sparked the slump, his departue follows those last month of metals executive general manager Geoff Billard, and exploration executive general manager Ross Fardon. Page 29.

Perth-based media magnate Jack Bendat says that unless the Golden West Network's exclusive programming arrangement with the Nine Network is dropped, a second commercial television licence for regional Western Australia will not be viable. Bendat has called on the Australian Broadcasting Authority to lift the A$10,000 deposit on bids for the new State commercial licence to between A$250,000 to A$500,000 to ensure the licence would go to a broadcaster with strong finances. Page 31.

Australian Provincial Newspapers chief executive Cameron O'Reilly's intense lobbying has resulted in the Federal Government agreeing to amend the cross-media laws leading up to its extensive review of media ownership. The so-called O'Reilly amendments will see the Government watering down the test which prevents a person owning a newspaper and radio station in the same area. Page 31.

Prime Minister John Howard has showed his annoyance of his own party's conduct on the tariff debate, and has called on backbenchers not to make ill-informed contributions leading up to the Productivity Commission's report on the car industry. Howard is aso irritated by reports of preselection manoeuvrings in the South Australian Liberal Party which are linked to the tariff row. Page 31.
THE AGE

Shares in Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation fell sharply yesterday, with preferred shares dropping 40 cents to A$5.20, and ordinary shares falling 22 cents to A$6.36, after Murdoch announced the company would pay A$940 million for United States-based Heriage Media Corporation. As part of the deal, News Corp will assume A$760 million of Heritage's debts.
Page B1.

The Federal Government's leading forecaster, the Australian Bureau of Agriculture and Resource Economics, says the drop in Australia's wheat exports will be balanced by a revival in the world wool price, and strong earnings from coal, gold and aluminium. While total exports are forecast at A$58.2 billion in 1996-97, exports should hit a record level of A$62.5 billion next year. Page B1.

The Gold Index fell 1.9 per cent yesterday following the West Australian Government's firmest indication yet that it will introduce a royalty on gold production. Prices of gold stocks fell, indicating investor concern of the cost impact of the royalty, gven that 70 per cent, or more than A$3 billion, of gold production takes place in Western Australia. Page B1.

In seeking finance for the A$190 million-A$253 million development of its Guelb Moghrein copper-gold project in Mauritania, West Australian, Perth-based company General Gold Resources NL has turned to the North American market. Under an agreement announced yesterday, General Gold will sell its 50 per cent interest in the project to Solomon Resources of Canada. Page B2.

The third quarter profit for BHP is expected to be driven at least 60 per cent above last year's result to A$340 million due to stronger oil prices for much of the February quarter, offset by slightly weaker copper prices for much larger volumes. Strengthin oil and minerals will be balanced by weak conditions plaguing the steel industry. Page B3.

National Australia Bank has made a rush for United States market share with its subsidiary, Michigan National Bank, allocating A$1.27 billion for new business lending. MNB, bought by NAB in 1995, has total assets of only US$9.5 billion. Page B3.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
